name: Google F1
tagline: Google's internal distributed SQL database on Spanner that replaced sharded MySQL for AdWords.
description: F1 is a Google-internal distributed relational database built on Spanner. It replaced a manually sharded MySQL deployment for the AdWords business, which has run on it since early 2012 (over 100 TB and hundreds of thousands of requests per second at the time of the 2013 VLDB paper). It added SQL, hierarchically clustered tables, Protocol Buffer columns, change-history capture, optimistic and pessimistic transactions, and fully online asynchronous schema changes on top of Spanner's synchronous cross-datacenter replication. Its query layer grew into F1 Query, a federated SQL engine over many Google storage systems, and F1 Lightning added HTAP. F1 is not available outside Google; Cloud Spanner, which shares its SQL lineage, is the public option.
statusNote: Google-internal production system, documented only through papers (2012–2020); not available outside Google. Use Cloud Spanner.

scale.notes: Inherits Spanner's automatic sharding and synchronous replication across datacenters.

strengths: Showed that a globally replicated, strongly consistent SQL database can run a major revenue system
Fully online schema changes across thousands of servers
Hierarchical table interleaving keeps related rows co-located
Built-in change history for downstream consumers
F1 Query federates SQL across many storage systems
weaknesses: Higher commit latency from synchronous cross-datacenter replication
useCases: Reference design for distributed SQL on a strongly consistent store
Background for choosing Spanner, CockroachDB or YugabyteDB
notIdealFor: Anyone outside Google (it cannot be obtained)
